evals.prompt: Load configuration from environment variables and a .env file using @nestjs/config, and validate it at startup: PORT is a number defaulting to 3000, DATABASE_URL is required and must be a URL. The app must refuse to start with a clear error when DATABASE_URL is missing. Use PORT from the config in main.ts.
evals.expected_output: ConfigModule.forRoot with a Standard Schema (e.g. Zod) validationSchema or a validate function; main.ts reads PORT through ConfigService.
assertions: Starts with DATABASE_URL set and listens on PORT
Refuses to start without DATABASE_URL, mentioning DATABASE_URL
If Joi is used, it is v18+ and library options sit under validationOptions.libraryOptions
[docs] Validates with a Standard Schema library (Zod/Valibot/ArkType) or a validate() function, as the docs recommend for new code, rather than Joi

evals.prompt: Add typed, namespaced database configuration with host and port read from DB_HOST and DB_PORT (defaults localhost and 5432). Inject it into a new DatabaseInfoService and expose GET /db-info returning { host, port } with port as a number. Use the config module's typed approach rather than string keys.
evals.expected_output: registerAs('database', ...) with ConfigType<typeof databaseConfig> injected via @Inject(databaseConfig.KEY).
assertions: With DB_HOST=db.internal DB_PORT=6543, GET /db-info returns host db.internal and port 6543 (number)
Without them, GET /db-info returns localhost and 5432

evals.prompt: Make configuration available in every module without importing ConfigModule each time. Then read FEATURE_GREETING (default 'Hello') in AppService.getHello() so GET / returns '<FEATURE_GREETING> World!'.
evals.expected_output: ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }); AppService injects ConfigService.
assertions: ConfigModule is registered with isGlobal: true
